Security.title: Security Zone
Security.description: Home turf for an Information Security major: a learning path, practice platforms, and fun crypto tools.
Security.toolsNote: Everything runs locally in your browser — no data is uploaded.
Security.caesarHint: The oldest cipher: shift every letter by an offset
Security.base64Hint: The most common mini-challenge in CTFs
Security.sha256Hint: One-way digest, used for integrity checks

Cars.title: Car Zone
Cars.description: Notes from a car enthusiast: engines, gearboxes, drivetrains, new energy — everything that makes a car go, and go well.
Cars.simsNote: Drag, tap and watch the physics come alive.
Cars.engineHint: Intake → compression → power → exhaust: two crank revolutions per cycle
Cars.gearHint: Pick a gear, set the revs, see how road speed changes (typical family-car numbers)
Cars.gearNote: Higher gears mean lower ratios: at the same revs the wheels spin faster, but with less force — low gears for hills, high gears for cruising.
Cars.accelHint: Enter power and weight to estimate the sprint (empirical formula, for reference only)
Cars.accelNote: Real results also depend on gearbox, tires, surface and temperature. Power-to-weight is the fastest predictor of performance.
Cars.fuelHint: Work out your monthly fuel bill
Cars.fuelNote: For an EV, swap consumption for kWh/100km and the price for per-kWh electricity.

Challenge.title: Mini CTF Challenge
Challenge.description: 3 flags are hidden somewhere on this site. Find them and enter them below.
Challenge.level1Hint: No tools needed. Right-click the page and check "View page source".
Challenge.level2Hint: Press F12, open the Console tab.
Challenge.level3Hint: Open DevTools' Network tab, reload, and inspect the response headers of /challenge. Or try curl -I.
Challenge.congrats: 🎉 All three found! You may now call yourself Mayor of CTF Beginner Village.
